chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from al-Khashshab from Ali ibn Asbat from whoever narrated:
"Regarding the gallbladders, there is no harm in eating them if they are mixed [with other permissible parts/meat]."
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat animal gallbladders in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling on the permissibility of consuming animal gallbladders (*jallat*), noting that they are acceptable when mixed with other parts, likely invoking the principle of *khalat* (mixing) to render the disliked element negligible. This reflects the Shia juristic approach to food purity, where the presence of a minor impure or disliked component does not invalidate the whole if it is sufficiently integrated with permissible matter. The hadith highlights the practical flexibility in dietary laws, distinguishing between distinct impurities and those that become acceptable through combination.
